Triggers.value: A specific temperature on the skin

Threat.value: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building
I notice potential weapons or dangerous objects in any environment

Memory.value: My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed.
The memory feels like it is happening right now rather than something that is over
The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to

Negative Appraisals.value: I feel dirty or contaminated because of what happened
The world is a dangerous place
My body has been permanently damaged by what happened

vignette: Señor García, a 67-year-old widowed prosecutor from a Latin American background, has been struggling with the aftermath of a sexual assault that occurred over six months ago. The event left him feeling profoundly shaken and marked by an overwhelming sense of vulnerability. Since the assault, Señor García experiences vivid memories that feel like they are happening in the present rather than something in the past. He often finds himself reliving the traumatic experience when he encounters specific triggers-being around children or a particular temperature on his skin can instantly transport him back to the moment of the assault. These triggers frequently lead to intense flashbacks, making it difficult for him to function normally at work and during daily activities. Señor García's memories are not just intrusive; they also reinforce his negative appraisals about himself and the world. He feels permanently contaminated and believes that his body has been irrevocably damaged by what happened. This conviction is so powerful that it fuels a deep sense of fear and anxiety, making him avoid unfamiliar places because he cannot assess the danger there. Whenever Señor García enters a new environment or even a familiar one, his first instinct is to scan for exits and notice potential weapons or dangerous objects around him. His negative appraisals about contamination and vulnerability further exacerbate his threat responses. He often finds himself overly vigilant, constantly on edge as if the world is a dangerous place where any person could pose a threat. This heightened state of awareness makes it difficult for him to relax or trust others, even those he once considered close friends. Señor García's work as a prosecutor has also been impacted by his condition. He avoids taking cases that involve children and often finds himself unable to focus during trials due to the intrusive memories and the fear they trigger. His colleagues have noticed changes in his behavior-his tendency to scan for exits and notice potential weapons makes him appear distant and preoccupied. The assault has left Señor García feeling deeply isolated. He had come to believe that he was permanently damaged and feared that this damage would always be visible to others, making it hard for him to maintain social connections. His sense of contamination and vulnerability often leads him to avoid situations where children are present or where he might encounter a specific temperature on his skin, as these triggers can immediately bring back the traumatic memories. Señor García's negative appraisals not only influence his threat responses but also intensify the vividness and intrusiveness of his memories. When he encounters triggers like being around children or feeling a particular temperature, it reinforces his belief that the world is dangerous and that he is vulnerable. This cycle has tightened over time, making it increasingly difficult for him to manage his symptoms. What finally brought Señor García to seek help was the realization that he could no longer function effectively in his role as a prosecutor or maintain meaningful relationships. He is most afraid of continuing to live in a constant state of fear and contamination, but he is also hopeful that with support and treatment, he can regain control over his life and find peace again. Señor García's current state reflects the complex interplay between his triggers, memories, negative appraisals, and threat responses. The specific symptoms he experiences are not just isolated reactions but form a self-reinforcing cycle that has significantly impacted his quality of life.
